programme: No single module unites these twelve. They fall into at least six unrelated programmes: MHC-II antigen presentation (RFX1, via CIITA/HLA-DRA/HLA-DMB/HLA-DOB/HLA-DPB1); neural-crest→Schwann/melanocyte specification (SOX10, via MPZ/MITF/ERBB3/DCT/MBP/GJB1/RET/EDNRB); Spemann-organizer/mesendoderm patterning (GSC, via BMP4/PAX3/MIXL1/FOXH1/CHRD); H3K79-methylation chromatin linked to MLL-leukemia (DOT1L, via IRF1/STAT1/MCL1/BCL2/MEIS1); midbrain-hindbrain patterning (EN2, via FGF8/WNT7B); circadian clock output (DBP, via PER1/PER2/ARNT/CYP7A1/CYP3A4); AP-2/estrogen-responsive epithelial identity (TFAP2C, via ESR1/ERBB2/ERBB3/EGFR/GREB1/GPER1); IL2/IL4 cytokine control (BCL6B); steroidogenic zinc-finger regulation (SALL3, via CYP11A1/TH/DNMT3A); AR-coactivator/ferritinophagy (NCOA4, via AR/KLK3/TFF1); autonomic/noradrenergic neuron specification (PHOX2B, via DBH/HAND1/HAND2/TH/ISL1); and REST-linked neurogenic chromatin (ZNF335). None of these target sets overlap, no two factors are known to sit in the same complex, and no retrieved paper places more than one of them together in either disease.
role_in_a: No shared programme to assign a role to. Only DBP has an on-topic hit in Cardiovascular_Disease (circadian regulation of blood-pressure fluctuation), and that is a single-factor, single-paper association, not evidence of a module.
role_in_b: Likewise, only EN2 has an on-topic hit in Uterine_Corpus_Endometrial_Carcinoma (a recurrence-free-survival RNA signature), an isolated factor-level association that does not connect to any of the other eleven factors or to DBP's cardiovascular finding.
shared_axis: There is no mechanism to propose: the two on-point findings (DBP in cardiovascular physiology, EN2 in endometrial prognosis) belong to unrelated biology (circadian/metabolic vs. developmental homeobox) and nothing in the record links them or any other pair of factors here to each other.
reasoning: The twelve factors are drawn from at least six distinct, non-interacting developmental/physiological programmes with no target overlap and no documented complex or pathway relationship between them; forcing a neural-crest or embryonic-TF story would still only cover SOX10/PHOX2B/EN2/GSC, and even those specify different neural-crest derivatives (melanocyte/Schwann vs. autonomic neuron vs. organizer vs. midbrain) rather than one lineage. Almost every retrieved paper is explicitly off-topic (melanoma, leukemia, prostate cancer, glioma, Paget disease, cholangiocarcinoma), and the two on-topic hits are single-factor, single-disease, and mechanistically unrelated to each other, so there is nothing here to build a cross-disease account on.
support: PMID 32105510 — places EN2 in Uterine_Corpus_Endometrial_Carcinoma only, as part of an RNA-based recurrence-free-survival signature, with no bearing on cardiovascular disease or the other eleven factors; PMID 34290536 — places DBP in Cardiovascular_Disease only, via circadian/hypoxia effects on blood-pressure dynamics, with no bearing on endometrial carcinoma or the other eleven factors.
how_to_falsify: Take matched cardiovascular-disease and endometrial-carcinoma patient cohorts and test whether any subset of these twelve factors (e.g., SOX10, PHOX2B, GSC, EN2) co-occupy shared regulatory elements (ChIP-seq/ReMap overlap beyond the sparse binding already reported) or show correlated expression across both tissues; if no cross-factor co-binding, co-expression, or physical interaction is found, that confirms the set is a coincidental collection of independently recurrent factors rather than a module, consistent with this verdict.
caveats: 48 patient-group comparisons across only 2 independent cohort pairs for blood vs. uterine/endometrial tissue — a small number of independent replicates behind the recurrence fractions. The single-view exclusions (TSG101, RUNX1, KAT5, etc.) were even less recurrent, so they are not a stronger alternative story. The tissue-generic exclusions (NFATC1, STAT5A/B, BCL6, BCL3, JUNB, PRDM1, ERG, E2F2, KLF6, CEBPG, CREB5) removed the expected blood/immune and vascular master regulators — their absence explains why the surviving set looks unusually developmental/heterogeneous rather than immune- or vascular-themed, and should not be read as those programmes being newly implicated.
